newsitem.title: UK: Funds upbeat on Europe on growth prospects - survey.
newsitem.headline: Funds upbeat on Europe on growth prospects - survey.

text.p: Sentiment towards continental European equities among fund managers globally has rebounded on improved prospects about European growth and profits, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.
The survey, conducted by Gallup, said managers were again looking to raise exposure in the region after a dip in confidence when the left came to power in France in June.

"There is a marked change of perception towards the outlook for continental European equity markets. Respondents are significantly more bullish on the near term outlook for European bourses," Merrill said.
It said its U.S. survey found bulls outnumbered bears by 38 percent on continental Europe compared to June when bulls matched bears.

It said the reversal was probably due to optimism about European activity and thus earnings per share growth rates. In the European survey, 98 percent of respondents were looking for stronger European growth and higher profits, and most felt this would not be accompanied by a rise in inflation.
The survey of continental European managers also said bulls outnumbered bears by 45 percent on a three month view on the region's equities.
The upbeat economic outlook is reflected in sector preferences, with capital goods sectors such as electrical and electronics favoured.
Continental European fund managers were also less negative on domestic bonds, it said.
It said 92 percent of continental European managers felt EMU would go ahead on time and include Germany and France.
The survey was carried out between July 4 and 9, covering 66 institutions responsible for funds totalling $550 billion.
